---
title: "Phylogenetic analysis of *Sarcoptes scabiei* var. *hominis* proteins"
format: docx
---

**Sarcoptes scabiei** var. **hominis** — phylogenetic trees derived from a
database of 531 retrieved proteins. Representative sequences were taken from
`.github/Sarcoptes_human_accessions.csv`: 64 representative accessions, each
standing in for a cluster of near-identical sequences (cluster sizes shown in
brackets after each accession). Full methods, code and reproducibility notes
are in `06-sarcoptes-coi-tree.html`.

## Figure 1

![Neighbour-joining tree of the 43 COI representatives](06-sarcoptes-coi-tree_files/figure-html/tree-plot-1.png)

**Figure 1. Neighbour-joining phylogeny of mitochondrial COI protein sequences
from *Sarcoptes scabiei* var. *hominis* sampled from human hosts (database
retrieved 531 proteins; 43 COI representatives shown).** The 43 representative
COI accessions were downloaded from NCBI, aligned with MAFFT (`--auto`), and
their amino-acid distances used to build an unrooted neighbour-joining tree in
ape. Tip labels give the GenBank accession and, in brackets, the number of
near-identical sequences the representative stands for. Numbers at internal
nodes are bootstrap support from 100 resamplings of alignment columns; green
values (≥ 70%) indicate well supported groups. **Tree scale:** branch lengths
are in substitutions per amino-acid site; the scale bar corresponds to 0.1.
Sequences are partial fragments (40–275 amino acids), so deep branches carry
low support; the tree is a first-pass clustering of the available human-host
COI sequences, not a definitive mite phylogeny.

## Figure 2

![Circular cladogram of all 64 representatives](06-sarcoptes-coi-tree_files/figure-html/circular-plot-1.png)

**Figure 2. Circular cladogram of all 64 representative protein sequences from
*Sarcoptes scabiei* var. *hominis* (database retrieved 531 proteins).**
Neighbour joining on Dayhoff protein distances, drawn with equal-length
branches in a circular layout so that all labels are legible. Each labelled
accession stands in for a cluster of near-identical sequences (cluster size in
brackets). The six highlighted accessions are AAS93675.1 (red), AAS93667.1
(orange), AAS93669.1 (purple), AAO15606.1 (blue), AAO15613.1 (green) and
CAL18242.1 (magenta). Because the set mixes different genes, the grouping
mainly separates protein types (COI vs allergens vs muscle proteins, etc.).
**Tree scale:** not applicable — branches are drawn with equal lengths for
legibility, so only the grouping (topology), not distances, is informative in
this figure.

## Methods summary

1. Representative accessions were read from
   `.github/Sarcoptes_human_accessions.csv` (64 representatives standing in
   for 531 sequences).
2. Protein sequences were retrieved from NCBI GenBank with the E-utilities
   `efetch` service.
3. Sequences were aligned with MAFFT (`--auto`).
4. Pairwise amino-acid distances (Dayhoff-type correction, gaps handled
   pairwise) were computed with ape's `dist.aa`.
5. Trees were built by neighbour joining (`ape::nj`) and drawn with
   `ape::plot.phylo` (rectangular for COI; circular cladogram for all 64).
6. Branch reliability was estimated by non-parametric bootstrap (100
   replicates of alignment columns).

## Choices made

- Kept only COI sequences for Figure 1 — alternative: one tree of all 64
  sequences, which mixes unrelated genes.
- Amino-acid (protein) distances with `dist.aa` — alternative: nucleotide
  distances with `dist.dna` (only protein sequences available).
- Neighbour joining — alternative: maximum likelihood (more rigorous, much
  slower).
- MAFFT `--auto` alignment — alternative: ClustalW, generally less accurate.
- Gaps handled pairwise in the distance — alternative: strip all gapped
  columns, which would discard most of this short alignment.
- 100 bootstrap replicates, ≥ 70% considered solid — alternative: 1,000
  replicates (tighter estimates, ~10× slower).
- Tree left unrooted — alternative: midpoint rooting, which assumes the two
  most distant sequences bracket the root.
- Cluster sizes shown in tip labels as `(n=…)` — alternative: circles scaled
  by `n`.
- Figure 2 drawn as a circular cladogram with equal-length branches —
  alternative: distance fan, unreadable because unrelated proteins sit on
  extremely long branches.
- Non-highlighted tips grey, each highlighted accession in its own colour —
  alternative: one colour for all six.
- Cluster sizes taken as given from the sheet (read by eye from a figure) —
  alternative: re-export the collapse table for exact counts.
